summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: "All vertebrates are chordates, but not all chordates are vertebrates." Cyclostomes are jawless ectoparasites that migrate from the sea into freshwater rivers to spawn (anadromous).

conceptBreakdown.content: Subphylum Vertebrata (Craniata) members possess an embryonic notochord that is replaced in the adult by a cartilaginous or bony **Vertebral Column**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.1 Class Cyclostomata (Jawless Primitive Vertebrates)
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.1 Class Cyclostomata (Jawless Primitive Vertebrates)
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Mouth & Jaws**: Jaws are **ABSENT** (Agnatha). Possess a suctorial, circular, jawless mouth armed with rasping horny epidermal teeth.
• **Ectoparasitic Habit**: Obligate ectoparasites on marine fishes; body is elongated, eel-like, smooth, and **devoid of scales and paired fins**.
• **Gills & Skeleton**: Possess **$6\text{--}15\text{ pairs}$ of pharyngeal gill slits** for respiration. Cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous; heart is 2-chambered (1 atrium, 1 ventricle) with closed circulation.
• **Anadromous Migration & Larva**: Marine adults migrate upstream to freshwater river beds to spawn (**Anadromous**). After spawning within a few days, adults die. Their free-swimming ciliated **Ammocoete Larva** undergoes metamorphosis and migrates back to the ocean.
• **Key Taxa**: *Petromyzon* (lamprey), *Myxine* (hagfish).
